_doc: Set pieces: authored layout recipes for famous Night City places (SetPieces, SetPieceGen). The book gives no floor plans, so a set piece is a recipe the generators follow: the place stays recognisable while the rooms vary per seed. Keys: name; locations {location id (data/world/locations.json): params that location adds, e.g. which structure is the target}; faction (the Security Code's faction, the default opposition); base {scene (scenes.json; its theme, doctrine and civilians), planner (SetPieceGen: plot = a building plot with its annexes, port = quays and anchored ships, compound = buildings round a court inside a perimeter wall, arena = a walled block of fake city from a district profile with the owner's production yard at the back)}; arena (w, h, floors, profile (districts.json), outside / forecourt / track (squares round the wall), yard (depth of the production yard), hatches (tunnel hatches: entrances reinforcements come up), tunnels {w, kind, posts} (a storey of tunnels under the set joining the hatches, a ladder up each: BasementGen), street_kind, yard_kind, dress [{piece, per: one per that many open squares}]); variants [{id, name, owner, note, security_code (the encounter's code and post holders for that variant), params (scene params over the recipe's), look}]: one drawn per seed (or overrides.variant by id), kept in the map's params; params (scene params; the caller's win); plot (the building plot: margin, front yard depth, side_yard (open ground beside the building), fence along the street (fence_mat), yard kind, zone and ground, front_ground (a lawn), approach {kind, zone, w} (a yard of its own over the path to the door), dress [{piece, count, area: front | lot}], flagpole, annexes behind or beside the main building, pool {w, d, gap, kind} (water on a deck behind the house), gatehouse (a guard booth inside the gate)); compound (court {w, d, kind, ground, zone}, buildings [{part, at [x, y] round the court, w along its entrance facade, d, floors, gap, entry}], margin, ground, zone, yard, wall_mat (1 concrete, 3 chain-link), booth, dress [{piece, count, area: court | yard}]); sites {part: {base: a sites.json site, then site keys that replace the base's (layout replaces key by key)}}: part main is the target building unless locations say otherwise; posts [{where: roof | deck | room:<kind>, part (_scene: the outdoor rooms), kind, count [a, b], weapon (the guard posted there carries it as their primary), cover (sandbags round the post), spread (anywhere in the room, not its middle)}]: posts the guards man first; props [{where (also top: the highest roof), part, piece (Furnish's or SetPieceGen.PIECES: cupola, flagpole, spire, turret, mast, funnel, columbarium, av), count, at: center | door}]; key_rooms {part (or _scene: the outdoor rooms): [room kinds every seed must have]}; anchors {objective kind: {room kind: score}} (a site part may carry its own; Encounter.secure_cell, which only reaches rooms without a locked security door, so anchors name staff-zone rooms; data uses the NET instead, eliminate needs no anchor); rules (special rules the engine honours: public_access, civilians, neutral_ground {name, part, hud, hud_broken}: the building's public floor is a house where nobody fights until the crew does, NeutralGround; free_for_all {faction, rank, count, blocks, keep_out}: a side at war with everyone roaming the map, FreeForAll; a rule's brief is a line for the job board and the gig's log, SetPieces.briefs); todo (rules the engine can't honour yet); look (tags; wall_crenels, graffiti_walls for the perimeter wall); a part's own look (SetPieceDressing: wall / roof {color, color2, pattern (11 brick), scale}, trim, roof_mark none, graffiti, crown, terrace_lights, crenels, pads, waterline, sign, flooded [room kinds]); cite; _why: which book detail each element follows and what is ours. Below the street: a site part asks for storeys under it with basement {storeys, flood {-k: share of that storey under deep water}, flood_rooms [program kinds], shafts (how many stairs go down), down_from} and lays them out with program bands -1, -2 ... (or basement for all), which share the plan's band depths so stair halls line up (BasementGen; the map's street level is then floor TacMap.basements). Program keys only set pieces use (Layouts.program): keep {floor: {bands: [first, last]} | {u: [from, to]}} keeps only those bands (or that share of the facade) on a storey, so upper floors step back and the roofs below become terraces; secret {group: note}: items tagged secret: group are built on one floor only, drawn per seed; mirror: false fixes the plan's handedness; an item's steady: true takes its exact share of the band (no jitter), so a central stair core sits on the same squares on every storey.

fort_sumter.name: Fort Sumter
todo: Gunslinger's Brennan Infiniti aerodyne cyberbike is set dressing on the roof pad; no vehicle rules yet.
Friends-only second floor: guards treat the crew as hostile there like anywhere off the public floor; no reputation/friendship check yet.
A US public school's courtyard plan (an E or H wing round a court): the program fills one rectangle.

Members only below ground: the basements are staff zone like the upper floor (guards treat the crew as hostile there, no membership check); both stair halls go down, so the security office is a post, not the only gate.
fort_sumter._why: Book (NC2045 p.143, South Night City #4), SC 10 DeadWoods Hardened Medium. Notes: ex-high school, abandoned during the 3rd Corporate War, now the DeadWoods' base. 1F: small auditorium, chow hall (cafeteria + kitchen), petition offices for locals (petition_office both sides of the lobby; public_access + civilians). 2F, for gang friends: rec room, ops centre, entertainment (a saloon bar, ours). Basement levels, members only: bunks, gym, gun range, armory, security office. Roof: sniper posts + pad for Gunslinger's prototype AV cyberbike. Bikes garaged behind the school (bike_garage annex). Ours: the members-only levels are a basement and sub-basement under the school (basement.storeys 2, program bands -1 / -2): B1 the security office at the foot of the stairs (a guard post), bunks (crew_quarters), a gym, washroom and crash room off a members' corridor; B2 the gun range with the armory beside it, deepest, and a gunsmith's workshop (staff zone, no keycard locks: a gang base, and so objectives can sit there); both stair halls carry down, the plan's bands shared so they line up; the school keeps its double-loaded hallway, two stair halls (two means of escape) and fenced yard; Gunslinger's own room upstairs (boss_room) and where captives are held are ours. Sniper nests are guard posts on the roof manned first, each guard handed a sniper rifle (the DeadWoods roster has no sniper block, so these are their own people with rifles) behind sandbags. Look (ours, from the American public-school type the book's "former high school" names): two storeys of red brick in running bond under a white stone cornice, a tar-and-gravel flat roof with a white bell cupola and clock over the entrance, a lit name band over the door, a front lawn with the flagpole flying the gang's colours, the asphalt schoolyard beside it with its old basketball court, all behind a chain-link fence; the DeadWoods' tags on the brickwork and their barricades (wrecks, jersey barriers, sandbags) on the lawn.

ziggurat_hq.name: Ziggurat Headquarters

secret.citinet: The CitiNet servers (data_vault) are built on one floor of the tower only, drawn per seed: their location is a closely guarded secret (NC2045 p.78).

todo: Tech squads rolling out of the bays as a response (NC2045 p.78) and the fire/EMS station answering an alarm: no responder hook for them yet; the station is a neutral building.
Public tours: the crew passes as visitors on the public floor and the plaza only while no alarm is up (public_access); no disguise or visible-weapon checks yet.

The curve is a stepped pyramid on the square grid: the front and both ends set back (two squares a side a storey, the front band at floor 4), the back stays sheer; one central stair and the lift (a second stair would need a second core).
ziggurat_hq._why: Book (NC2045 p.78, Upper Marina #40), SC 10 Ziggurat Security Hardened Heavy. Notes: curved megatower. Low floors: service-vehicle bays + tech squads (vehicle_bay with service door; ready room, workshops, dispatch on 2F). Mid floors: dev labs, CitiNet/Data Pool control, sales (lab, server_room, content_control, bullpen, meeting). Upper: key offices (exec_office), CEO UR's suite at the apex (ceo_suite alone on top). 1F public: Net museum + press auditorium (net_museum, auditorium, lobby: public_access + civilians; security post before the lifts = first restricted door). CitiNet server floor kept secret (data_vault on one of three floors, drawn per seed, so a data gig must find it). Fire/EMS company in its own building at the base (fire_station annex). Ours: the curve is a ziggurat (the company's name; the stepped-pyramid tower type): two full podium storeys, then each storey set back on the front and both ends round a central stair-and-lift core (Ching: a stacked core under setbacks), the step roofs planted terraces edged in light, gold banding at every floor line and a lit spire crowning the top storey, the plaza, the security post and lift lobby as the first restricted door, the band layout and room sizes.

main_port.name: Main Port and Flotsam

sakata_maru.name: Sakata Maru (ex-Arasaka munitions ship, Port administration)

rose.name: The Rose (submarine, Thelas comms hub and the Pilots' Club)

lund.name: OGV Lund (container hulk, still being salvaged)

todo: The Sakata Maru's anti-aircraft guns are deck mounts with a gunner each; they don't yet shoot down AVs (Trauma Team, MaxTac) arriving over the port.
Flotsam's shifting geography (ships come and go daily) is the per-seed layout of the floats; no boats to steal or sail.
Quay depths, the rail link to the Yard and the dry dock are flavour (rail ground, a construction site); no tide or crane-operation rules.
main_port._why: Book (NC2045 p.153-154, Port of Night City #5 Flotsam and #7 Main Port; both SC 10 Thelas Marines Hardened Heavy). Main Port notes: Q1 hand-unloaded, no cranes (pallets, crates); Q2-3 bulk cargo, 2 container cranes each, rail to the Yard (4 cranes, rail strip, container yard, moored freighter); Q4 newest, cranes + cargo-drone hangar and control (drone_hangar + control room); Q5 half built (construction site). Flotsam notes: small craft, kelongs, pontoons and floats tied to three bay wrecks: OGV Lund (drifting container hulk, fewer than 2,000 of 5,000 boxes salvaged: decayed, boxes on deck), the Rose (old sub; Thelas comms hub run by Netrunners; tug pilots' club: comms_room, server_room, Pilots' Club bar), Sakata Maru (ex-Arasaka munitions ship, now port admin: Calypso + senior staff, AA guns added: admin superstructure with bullpen, offices, Calypso's exec_office, bridge above, old magazines as armories, AA mounts on deck). Main Port location targets the freighter, Flotsam the Sakata Maru. Ours: one map for both (Flotsam lies in the bay off the quays, joined to the port by a long float walkway), the quay order west to east, the Sakata Maru dressed as the warship she was built as (haze-grey hull with a red boot-top at the waterline, a long raked bow, the stepped superstructure amidships with the bridge at its front, a lattice mast and funnel on top, a gun turret on the fore and after decks beside the AA mounts), the kelongs' positions and the fenced port gate on the road.

norcal_potentilla.name: The Potentilla (NorCal Military Base)
todo: The compound sinking underground on its elevators (NC2045 p.184): no lockdown event yet; it would end the gig or seal the petals.

The rest of the base: the Main Gate (the only way in for outsiders, MP credential checks; p.182) as an approach map or a disguise check, MP escorts for visitors (p.181), the airfield, the Motor Pool's tanks and ACPA (p.183).

Four petals are other units' HQs built from the plain office site; only the intelligence petal has a program. Each could get its own (the 157th's flight ops, the 223rd's armour, Task Force 384's naval ops).
norcal_potentilla._why: Book (NC2045 p.184, NorCal Military Base #13), SC 11 COG MPs Hardened Heavy (in play the MPs hold the posts via the location code). Notes: five buildings round a courtyard, flower-shaped; four unit HQs (TF 384, 157th TAS, 223rd Bn, 120.8th Engr Bn); the fifth houses the small units incl. military intelligence and drone ops (our target petal, at the head: control_room, ops_center, server_room, archive, data vault). Court: base memorial + small columbarium (prop at centre, honour guard). Fortified: perimeter wall, gate booth, MP checkpoint at the petal door. Why this site (p.178-185 lists 17): the Main Gate (p.182) is a gatehouse and lot, not a map; airfield, Motor Pool and docks are open ground; the Potentilla is the base's brain (gigs: data theft, sabotage) and five buildings round a court give several approaches, a killing ground and objectives in any petal. Ours: the petals' sizes and their places round the court (head petal north, two at the sides, two flanking the gate path), the Biotechnica Realgrass court (the base's parade ground uses it, p.184), the drone/intel petal's rooms, the flagpoles, and the base's COG soldiers holding the posts (the location's owner).

maxtac_hq.name: MAX-TAC Headquarters

main.name: MAX-TAC HQ: offices, intelligence and comms

east_tower.name: MAX-TAC HQ east tower (vehicles, AVs, repair bays)

barracks.name: MAX-TAC HQ south wing (front desk, barracks, training)

todo: AVs on the east tower's pads are cover and set dressing: a MAX-TAC AV launching as the response (p.144) isn't tied to the pads yet.
The castle's curtain wall is solid wall a storey high (perimeter fence material: concrete); no wall-walk to stand on.
Hammerman tending his roses: no named NPC in the garden.
maxtac_hq._why: Book (NC2045 p.144-145, South Night City #9): MAX-TAC's headquarters, Security Code 11 MAX-TAC Hardened Heavy: a fortified castle with a protected, hidden garden at its centre, where Hammerman is said to tend roses himself (the courtyard, walled in by the four wings, its planters the roses; zoned secure, so only reached through the gaps between the wings); the east tower holds the vehicles from Gorgon security vans to Herakles AVs plus repair bays (east_tower: vehicle bays and a workshop on the ground floor, a workshop and dispatch above, AVs parked on its roof pads); the west tower one of the best armories outside the NorCal base (west_tower, three storeys: a checkpoint, armories, a gun range, ready rooms); between them meeting rooms, intelligence posts, communication centres, clinics, tech workshops, training, offices and barracks (the north wing, the target: comms, ops_center for intelligence, a clinic's recovery room, offices, Hammerman's exec_office, a workshop and the server room; the south wing on the street: front desk, interview room, gym, gun range and barracks). Ours: the castle as four crenellated wings round the garden inside a crenellated curtain wall with one gate and its booth, which wing holds what between the towers, the yellow trim (MAX-TAC's livery), snipers on the armory tower.

trauma_team_tower.name: Trauma Team Tower
todo: Dispatch and the executive offices are in the subbasement in the book: no storeys below the street, so they sit behind the security post at the back of the ground floor.
AVs on the launch pads are cover and set dressing; a squad launching from its bay as the response, and the air-control tower directing it, aren't modelled.
Every Trauma Team employee armed on duty (p.196): the medtechs and pilots on the roster carry guns; no unarmed hospital staff to tell apart.
trauma_team_tower._why: Book (NC2045 p.195, Watson Development #32): Trauma Team Tower, Security Code 10 Lazarus Hardened Heavy (Lazarus guards it, p.196: every Trauma Team employee is also armed on duty), the base of the Night City rapid-response teams and the regional HQ for the Pacifica Confederation. Facilities as printed: an exclusive client-only hospital (ground-floor client reception and an ER intake, surgeries, recovery wards, labs, a cold store and private suites on floors 2-3: public_access only in the reception), AV maintenance and launch bays for each squad (the tower steps back above the hospital and each step is a launch terrace with a pad and a parked AV, the squads' bays opening onto it on floor 4, their ready room and the maintenance workshop on floor 5), a tactical air control tower (the set-back top storey: control_room and comms_room), and dispatch and the executive offices buried in the subbasement, where the operators run the response (dispatch_office, control_room and exec_office behind the security post at the back of the ground floor: no basements, see todo). Ours: the stepped massing round a central core, white walls with TT-blue trim, pads lit in blue.

totentanz.name: Totentanz (Burleson Tower)

neutral_ground.name: TOTENTANZ
neutral_ground.brief: TOTENTANZ: NO FIGHTING ON THE FLOOR. Maelstrom's bouncers keep the peace in the club; start something where they can see it and the whole house turns on you. Out of their sight, anything goes.
neutral_ground._cite: NC2045 p.94: calm on most nights because Warlock wants buyers coming back; the risk is outside, beyond the bouncers' view. No mechanics given.
neutral_ground._house_rule: HOUSE-RULE: the club's public rooms on the ground floor are the house. Guards posted there stay neutral to the crew (no spotting, no joining a fight they didn't see) and the rest of Maelstrom holds fire at crew standing in them; the crew's first attack inside, or one a bouncer has clear sight of (15 squares, any direction), ends it for the gig and rouses the bouncers and every guard in the tower.

todo: Anyone you angered inside following you out to shank you (p.94): the house holds its fire at crew on the club floor, but nobody inside remembers a slight once you leave.
Burleson Tower is held up by Maelstrom's repairs: the broken top two storeys are set back and the walls breached (decay); no collapse rules.
Patrons come to bargain for tech and drugs (p.94): no trading with them.
totentanz._why: Book (NC2045 p.94, Hot Zone #11): Totentanz, Security Code 9 Maelstrom Hardened Heavy, the Hot Zone's 'castle': the club and its home, the damaged Burleson Tower, which Maelstrom rescued, keeps standing, guards from looters and runs; they fight anyone trying to rehab the blocks around it. No cover charge, dim lights, the Armageddon in a rusty can; mostly peaceful inside, Warlock wants people to come and bargain; once you leave and are out of the bouncers' sight, anyone you angered may shank you. So: the club on the ground floor is public (foyer with a bouncer posted, dance floor, bar; public_access with a crowd of patrons, the civilians), the approach from the street to the door is a public plaza, the rubble lots round the tower are Maelstrom's staff ground with lookouts posted in them, and the tower above is theirs (crash rooms, workshops, an armory, stashes, Warlock's boss_room on the fourth floor). Ours: the tower's size and five storeys, the broken top (the upper two storeys stand on part of the plan, their roofs rubble-strewn terraces), breached walls (decay), the red Maelstrom tags and neon sign, lookouts on the roof. The peace inside is rules.neutral_ground (NeutralGround): the club's public rooms are the house, the foyer's bouncer neutral until the crew fights in the house or in a bouncer's view; how that ends (one attack, the whole tower roused) is a HOUSE-RULE.

eurasiabank_plaza.name: Eurasiabank Plaza (the sunken bank)
todo: Six storeys below the plaza (p.93): the map is the pit floor with the stump's three exposed storeys on it and two drowned bank storeys below grade; the storeys between are left out.
Flooded squares are deep water (T.WATER, impassable); the rest of a flooded room is a wet sheen. No wading or drowning rules yet.

The Crater (#2, the old Arasaka HQ pit, Reckoner prophets and their 'pure souls') and Dark Zone One (#4, the jamming and the snipers) are other Hot Zone ruins this recipe could serve with their own guards.
eurasiabank_plaza._why: Book (NC2045 p.93, Hot Zone #6), SC 2 NCPD Hardened Heavy (help almost never comes). Notes: the tower sank rather than fell in the nuke, six storeys now below ground, the top half collapsed; sunken floors partly flooded, bigger than expected, vaults/servers/files inside, dangerous, a magnet for doomba rumours and lost explorers (rescue anchors in the vaults, snatch anchors on vault + counting room for cash and gold). Unowned; Maelstrom's Diggers under Ripper scavenge and defend the turf (p.95). HOUSE-RULE: params.security 2 rather than the code's level 3, because the Diggers hold the place, not the NCPD. Ours: the map is the bottom of the pit, a gravel and rubble crater floor round the stump's three exposed storeys (a file-store floor at the pit floor, the Diggers' camp of squat rooms and a stash on the two broken storeys above); below grade (basement.storeys 2) the drowned bank: B1 the banking hall and counting room over files and servers, B2 the vault level deepest, vaults either side of a counting room; flood shares 12% and 30% of each storey's floor in deep water pools (doorways, stairs and every room's way to the stair stay dry, half of every room too), the rest of those rooms a wet sheen; Diggers posted in the sunken banking hall, the collapsed parts of each storey rubble-strewn terraces to climb over, breached walls and holed roofs (decay), lookouts on the stump and in the rubble.

combat_zone.name: The Combat Zone

free_for_all.brief: THE COMBAT ZONE: CONTESTANTS LOOSE ON THE SET. Implanted and desperate, they fight anyone they meet, Net54's people included.
free_for_all._cite: NC2045 p.216: fifty contestants, stripped, sedated and implanted, wake alone on the set and scavenge for gear, then fight a three-day battle royale. No stat block given.
free_for_all._house_rule: HOUSE-RULE: a gig meets 3-5 of the fifty, Boostergangers (CPR core p.412: fragile street fighters with a poor pistol and claws, the nearest printed block to scavenging amateurs with implants), one side against the crew, Net54 and anyone who answers a call, roaming the set (not the bunker or the production yard). They are one side, not fifty: they don't fight each other.

todo: The MIST (p.216): out of scope, descoped by the owner. The set plays as an ordinary map.

Contestants: a handful of the fifty roam the set as one side (rules.free_for_all); they don't fight each other, scavenge gear or enter later, and the rescue's captive (one of them, in the bunker's prep cells) is still a plain captive.
Drones: Network 54's camera drones and MAX-TAC flyovers (authorised to snipe trespassers when the set is not filming) have no flying units yet; camera masts and ground cameras stand in for them.

Tunnels: one storey of guard tunnels (arena.tunnels) joins the hatches, a ladder up each; reinforcements still arrive at the hatches rather than walking the tunnels in, and the tunnels are not dug round the bunker.

Turrets fire on their own (Turret, CPR core p.214) and a Netrunner holding their node turns them on Net54; the book's other mounts (flamethrower, dartgun, VH pistol, heavy SMG) and countering one by hand (Electronics/Security Tech DV17) aren't modelled: every turret carries an assault rifle.
combat_zone._why: Book (NC2045 p.216, New Westbrook #5): Network 54's walled film set, a fake urban wasteland; SC 10 Net54 Security, Medium; own guards, drones, auto-turrets and cameras; extra guards in the tunnels below while filming; implanted contestants. Ours: the wall is the map's perimeter, the street past its front, a checkpoint booth at the main gate, a service door near a front corner. Inside a gravel track, the set is a Combat Zone district (DistrictGen); its streets are one outdoor room dressed as a battlefield (rubble, wrecks, barricades) under cameras, camera masts and turrets. At the back, behind a chain-link fence, the production yard (its own gate) and the bunker, the target: broadcast gallery, uplink (roof dish), footage servers, prep cells and surgery (the rescue's captive), producers' offices upstairs, overwatch on the roof. Gigs: rescue, sabotage; other kinds anchor in the bunker. Tunnel hatches with a guard post each lead down to a storey of guard tunnels (BasementGen). Contestants roam the set as a side at war with everyone (rules.free_for_all, FreeForAll; count and block a HOUSE-RULE). Turrets use the core book's numbers (Turret, CPR core p.214). The MIST is out of scope (descoped by the owner).

the_estates.name: The Estates

variants.name: Artyom Sokolov's estate
variants.note: Zhirafa's CEO keeps estates like this round the world as a show of wealth; nobody has seen him sleep here.

variants.name: Denny's estate
variants.note: The ex-drummer of Samurai and Mastermind; her ex Henry sleeps off benders here now and then.

variants.name: Eran Malour's estate
variants.note: The mostly retired gun designer tinkers with new designs in his workshop; his granddaughter Marie-Louise (Netrunner 4) lives with him.

variants.name: Kerry Eurodyne's estate
variants.note: The rock legend owns it but is seldom here, or in Night City at all.

variants.name: Franklin M'bolu's estate
variants.note: Orbital Air's man on the spaceport project; last year someone sprayed 'Save Morro Rock' over his outer walls.

variants.name: Heather Stein's estate
variants.note: Biotechnica's Realgrass inventor, ex-president of the HOA, campaigning to take the gavel back.

variants.name: Jami Tealov's estate
variants.note: SovOil's Night City chief; his estate borders Petrochem's man Brentwood's.

variants.name: Karen Davies' estate
variants.note: Pol-Bud's regional director and the HOA's president: every centimetre keeps to the HOA's rules.

variants.name: Michiko Sanderson's estate
variants.note: The one estate guarded by Danger Gal, not Lazarus.

variants.name: Mister Kernaghan's estate
variants.note: The city's top high-end Fixer: whatever the residents want, he gets.

variants.name: Billy Joe Brentwood's estate
variants.note: Petrochem's Night City chief; his estate borders SovOil's man Tealov's.

variants.name: UR's estate
variants.note: Ziggurat's CEO runs the place with drones instead of servants, all under what may be the city's most elaborate NET Architecture.

todo: Lazarus drones over the grounds: no flying units; cameras, floodlights and automated turrets on the lawns stand in (the turrets fire on their own, Turret, and a Netrunner can turn them; every one mounts an assault rifle).
Decontamination sprayers: an arch over the drive inside the gate, dressing only (no gas rules for it).
Sprawling multi-building complexes and neighbouring estates (Tealov's borders Brentwood's): one mansion per map with its garage, gatehouse and pool.
Each owner's own security on top of Lazarus (the book's 'whatever else the owner buys') and UR's drone servants: only UR's NET is tougher (net_threat).
the_estates._why: Book (NC2045 p.235, Executive Zone #1): about twenty estates, from compact multilevel mansions to sprawling multi-building complexes, each guarded by Lazarus drones, automated turrets and decontamination sprayers plus whatever security the owner adds; Security Code 10 Lazarus, Hardened Heavy; the guide confirms twelve owners (A-L), Michiko Sanderson's guarded by Danger Gal (Security Code 10, Hardened Heavy) instead. Each gig draws one estate (variants: the owner, a line about them, the estate's Security Code; Sanderson's brings Danger Gal to the posts and the response; UR's NET is tougher; M'bolu's outer walls carry the 'Save Morro Rock' tags). Ours: one mansion per map, the villa site (growth layout) two or three storeys in white render under a slate roof on a landscaped lawn behind a concrete wall with one gate, a gatehouse just inside it, a fountain and planters on the front lawn, trees round the grounds, a pool on a deck in the back garden, a garage with a workshop beside the house; Lazarus patrols, cameras, floodlights and turrets on the grounds (the turrets shoot on their own: Turret, CPR core p.214); a decon arch over the drive. Objectives: the owner (assassinate) in a bedroom or the living room, a hostage held in a bedroom, the target's data in the study, sabotage in the kitchen or garage.
